sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's nickel processing boom is creating captive demand for renewable power, insulating local players from global rate sensitivity.
Domestic policy certainty under the new administration is accelerating project approvals for geothermal and solar, favoring first-movers like TPIA and BRPT.
US climate-tech names face headwinds from higher-for-longer rates and trade policy uncertainty, widening the performance gap with Indonesia-focused renewables.
sectors.ai: Despite the sector's aggregate decline, selective Indonesian names like TPIA and BRPT show strong relative outperformance, signaling that domestic policy tailwinds and project execution are driving divergence from global headwinds. Focus on these local champions as they benefit from Indonesia's nickel downstreaming and captive renewable power demand, while avoiding US-exposed names.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rural consumption recovery is accelerating as government social aid disbursements and pre-Lebaran cash flows boost demand for staple goods in lower-tier cities and villages.
Halal-certified and local-brand FMCG products are gaining market share from multinationals, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward value-for-money and religious compliance.
E-commerce penetration in Indonesia's consumer staples is still under 5%, creating a structural growth runway for companies that invest in direct-to-consumer digital channels and last-mile logistics.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's consumer sector shows flat aggregate performance but a clear rotation into smaller-cap names (AGAR, GRMN, ECII) with double-digit gains, signaling selective bottom-fishing ahead of Lebaran. Focus on niche FMCG players with strong rural distribution and low institutional ownership, as they offer asymmetric upside if consumption data surprises positively in Q2.
